title: Design the intervention sensor with zoom-in and zoom-out analysis
summary: I read this as a request for a written design of an intervention sensor, for the owner and later Athena roles. It follows the BRIEF.md 2026-10-15 addendum: interventions wake Athena, and each event is analysed zoomed in and as patterns zoomed out. The design fits roadmap RM-3 and is built later, not now.

defaults_applied.how: Deliver a design doc with alternatives before any implementation.
Design claims cite repo files and decisions; numbers are labeled.
One focused design doc plus index links only; no code.
Criteria check the content of the zoom-in and zoom-out reasoning and the trigger, not just that a file exists.
The doc must state that a quiet sensor is not success.
cargo test and clippy run to confirm nothing broke.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: turn the 2026-10-15 BRIEF.md addendum into a written design for an intervention sensor with zoom-in and zoom-out reasoning. The audience is the owner/operator and later Athena roles that will build it.

The 'designed' default applies: this is a significant design, so the change is a design doc first, without code. A later job builds the sensor, as with docs/design/socratic-review.md, which is designed but not built.
The design fits the roadmap as an extension of RM-3 (close the intervention loop) and shares the introspection work in crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs.
BRIEF.md is owner-protected and is not edited.
The decision number is the next free D-number in docs/decisions.md, which I did not determine.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new design doc docs/design/intervention-sensor.md defines the sensor: what counts as an intervention signal, which existing records and sources feed it (the intervention log, D27 capture, introspection, watcher), and what 'wakes Athena' means as a concrete trigger and the job it starts. Each claim cites a file or decision.

The doc has a zoom-in section (one event: what happened, the gap, root cause, the fix, per the introspection-on-every-correction addendum) and a zoom-out section (patterns across interventions, goals, and BRIEF.md). It states how the two are combined, with one worked example taken from a real logged intervention in the repo.

The doc states the operator-to-Athena transition: what the operator logs by hand today, what Athena notices itself, and the order of automation. It lists alternatives considered and the reasons for the choice. It marks any numbers as measured or estimated.

The doc is tied to existing plans without conflict: it names the roadmap step RM-3 and the requirements-map rows OM-5 to OM-9, and it keeps BRIEF.md, the auditor/warden protected-file rules and 'not a database' unchanged. docs/design/roadmap.md and docs/decisions.md link to it, with a new decision entry in the existing D-number format. CHANGELOG.md gets one line.

The doc defines checkable done-when signals and failure signals for the sensor, for example a noticed intervention that the operator did not log. It states that an empty or quiet sensor is not success.
Run `cargo test` and `cargo clippy` from the repo root. Both pass, and any existing test that checks docs or decisions numbering or links, if present, still passes.

out_of_scope: Implementing the sensor in Rust code
Editing BRIEF.md or the owner's protected files
Building the auditor or warden roles
departures: Slightly lower p_reading_accepted: the request is vague about whether a design or an implementation is wanted.
